items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: It was in Stanley Dance's book, the interview with Clarke Terry.

ctx.x: Well, anytime you put a label on something, other people pick it up and who knows.

I presume that you are familiar with Clarke Terry's account of his joining your band, the first time he played a solo? It was in Stanley Dance's book, the interview with Clarke Terry. Do you know -- do you remember this? Clarke says, 'Charlie Barnet called me from California while I was working the Riviera, a big plush sort of place where Ellington swears he originally wrote, 'Sophisticated Lady.' I didn't know a soul in Charlie's band and the only person I knew in L.A. was Gerald Wilson. He took me over to where…

or something like that, and it wasn't too difficult, but it was a big chance to take, on the air, coast to coast. Ellington does things like that too. I stayed with the band for one of the happiest years of my life, until Charlie got lonesome for his swimming pools, private plane and yacht. Charlie's the most wonderful person in the world."
